_meta.title: wiki-sourced ML36 augment tier (#260)
_meta.note: gear-planner's crafting.json (verified against upstream master 2026-08-12) tops out at ML32 in every color pool, but the wiki's Category:Minimum level 36 augments holds the 63 top-tier sale augments (Diamond/Ruby/Sapphire/Topaz). Without them every ML36 solve slots one tier low. This shard is the wiki-sourced gap fill, injected into the same color pools so downstream processing (color normalization, fits_slots, verification) treats them exactly like natives.
_meta.vocabulary_rule: Each entry's affix (name, type) is anchored to its highest gear-planner SIBLING in the same color pool (recorded per entry) and MUST match it at build time — the vocabulary is gear-planner's, per the structural-sourcing rule, so 'Sapphire of Protection +12' emits Armor Class/Deflection like its +11 sibling (the wiki's 'Protection bonus' wording IS the Deflection bonus — 169 worn affixes already use this vocabulary). Only the VALUE is new, and it must appear verbatim in the recorded tooltip.
_meta.stale_guard: The build FAILS when (a) an entry's name appears in the upstream pool — gear-planner added the tier, retire this shard; (b) an entry's sibling vanishes or its affix vocabulary moves; (c) an entry's value is absent from its own recorded tooltip. A shard that cannot go stale unnoticed is the only kind worth having (#207).
_meta.evidence_rule: Every entry carries the verbatim item-page description (the rendered slotted-effect tooltip) and its wiki URL. Harvested 2026-08-12, same-origin from a ddowiki tab, two batched revisions calls.

Ruby of Shock (10d6).reanchor_note: #374/U4 — re-anchored `Shock` -> `Electrifying` on the wiki's own wording. The ITEM is named Ruby of Shock; the ENCHANTMENT is not. https://ddowiki.com/page/Item:Ruby_of_Shock_(10d6) reads `Enchantments: Electrifying 10` and files the page under `Electrifying 10 items`, so `Electrifying` is what a player reads on the tooltip. KTD1 says match the tooltip, so here that means ADOPTING upstream's name rather than defending ours — our `Shock` was the stale spelling, not the canonical one.
